ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.summary: Mathlib already contains all of CA.0 (gcd and Bézout, factorization, congruences, the Chinese remainder theorem including the non-coprime form, valuations, arithmetic functions, Dirichlet convolution and Möbius inversion) and much of CA.1–CA.4: Gauss and Jacobi sums, quadratic and Jacobi reciprocity, Bernoulli numbers, binomial identities and number families, resultants, discriminants and irreducibility criteria, Pell equations, two- and four-square theorems, Fermat for n = 3, 4 and Frobenius numbers. Mathlib and Tau Ceti together already supply every number-field invariant CA.5 hands off (integral bases, units, class groups and explicit class numbers, relative discriminants, Frobenius, Dedekind–Kummer), and CA.6–CA.7 start from Mathlib's Mahler measure, house, Kronecker and Northcott theorems, the rational normal basis theorem and Tau Ceti's K₀. Genuinely missing: power residue symbols, Hilbert symbols and any higher reciprocity law; Euler numbers, automatic and Farey sequences, Christol's theorem, general companion matrices and rational generating functions; Hermite normal form, Smith normal form beyond nonsingular integer matrices, rational canonical form and effective ideal algorithms; the three-square theorem, exponential equations and Egyptian fractions; Pisot and Salem numbers and the Smyth/Dobrowolski bounds; and all integral Galois-module theory (group-ring structure of 𝓞_L, locally free class groups, Noether, Hilbert–Speiser, Fröhlich–Taylor, orders).

targets.target: gcd, Bézout identity and the (extended) Euclidean algorithm
targets.note: The extended Euclidean algorithm is computable (`Nat.xgcd`, `EuclideanDomain.xgcd` under `[DecidableEq R]`) and Bézout holds in every Euclidean domain and Bézout domain; `Nat.gcd` itself is in core Lean.

targets.target: Prime factorization: existence and uniqueness
targets.note: For ℕ as a list of primes or a finsupp (`n ≠ 0`), and up to associates in any UFD; every PID is a UFD (instance).

targets.target: Congruences and residue rings
targets.note: Congruence on ℕ and ℤ, the ring ZMod n with its dictionary to congruences, Euler–Fermat, and congruence modulo a submodule.

targets.target: Chinese remainder theorem for coprime moduli and pairwise-coprime families
targets.note: Computable ℕ versions for two moduli and finite families, the ring isomorphism ZMod (mn) ≃ ZMod m × ZMod n, and the ideal-theoretic CRT for pairwise comaximal ideals of any commutative ring.

targets.target: Chinese remainder theorem at non-coprime moduli with the compatibility hypothesis a ≡ b mod gcd(m,n)
targets.note: `Nat.chineseRemainder'` takes exactly the hypothesis `a ≡ b [MOD gcd n m]` and returns a solution below lcm(n,m); uniqueness mod lcm holds over ℕ and ℤ. Stated for natural-number residues (a public ℤ-existence form and the fibre-product form R/(I∩J) ≅ R/I ×_{R/(I+J)} R/J are not stated).

targets.target: p-adic valuations, multiplicities and Legendre's formula for factorials
targets.note: Valuations on ℕ, ℤ and ℚ, multiplicity in any monoid, Legendre's formula in both the sum form and the digit-sum form (p−1)v_p(n!) = n − s_p(n); adic valuations of Dedekind domains are `IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intValuation`.

targets.target: Arithmetic functions (σ_k, φ, μ, Λ, ω, Ω, d) and multiplicativity
targets.note: σ_k, μ, Λ, ω (`cardDistinctFactors`), Ω and the divisor count are all defined with their multiplicativity; φ is `Nat.totient` with coprime multiplicativity, though not bundled as an `ArithmeticFunction`. Zero cases follow Mathlib's convention f 0 = 0.

targets.target: Dirichlet convolution and the ring of arithmetic functions
targets.note: Mathlib's convolution is the multiplication of the (commutative) semiring of arithmetic functions, with Dirichlet inverses when f 1 is invertible; Tau Ceti extends convolution to functions on nonzero ideals of a number field.

targets.target: Möbius inversion, instantiated at divisor sums
targets.note: (∀ n > 0, ∑_{d|n} f d = g n) ↔ (∀ n > 0, ∑ μ(x) g(y) = f n) over any ring, with additive-group and multiplicative versions and poset Möbius inversion; Tau Ceti adds ideal Möbius inversion (`TauCeti.IdealArithmeticFunction.convolution_one_eq_iff`).

targets.target: General finite-sum and multiplicative identities for divisor sums
targets.note: ∑_{d|n} φ(d) = n, ζ * pow k = σ_k, ∑_{d|n} Λ(d) = log n and multiplicativity of divisor sums over coprime factors are all proved.

duplicates.note: AN.0 also 'develops arithmetic functions' (with Dirichlet series, Euler products and summation), overlapping this layer's arithmetic-function and convolution targets.
Its §2.2 states Möbius inversion and Dirichlet convolution again, for arithmetic functions on ideals, identified with Mathlib's `ArithmeticFunction ℂ` convolution.

targets.target: Finite cyclic groups, cyclicity of (ℤ/n)ˣ and primitive roots
targets.note: (ℤ/n)ˣ is cyclic iff n ∈ {1,2,4,p^k,2p^k} (odd p), finite subgroups of units of a domain are cyclic, and a cyclic group has φ(d) elements of order d. The explicit decomposition of (ℤ/2^k)ˣ into cyclic factors is not stated.

targets.target: Power residues: the n-th power residue criterion and n-th power residue symbols (mod p and in number fields)
targets.note: Only the quadratic case exists (Euler's criterion over ZMod p and finite fields); the number of d-th powers in a cyclic group, the Kummer map with kernel (Kˣ)ⁿ and the Frobenius action σζ = ζ^{N𝔭} are ingredients. Missing: the general criterion a^{(q−1)/gcd(n,q−1)} = 1 and any n-th power residue symbol.

targets.target: Gauss sums and Jacobi sums with their norm and product identities
targets.note: Over any finite commutative ring with a primitive additive character: g(χ,ψ)g(χ⁻¹,ψ⁻¹) = #R for χ ≠ 1, g² = χ(−1)#F for quadratic χ, and J(χ,φ) = g(χ)g(φ)/g(χφ) when χφ ≠ 1. The trivial-character cases are separate lemmas; |g|² = q is two lines from these, not a named lemma.

targets.target: Quadratic reciprocity for Legendre and Jacobi symbols, with the supplementary laws at −1 and 2
targets.note: For distinct odd primes and for odd positive integers (Jacobi), with (−1/p) = χ₄(p) and (2/p) = χ₈(p); Mathlib has no Kronecker symbol (Tau Ceti assembles prime-discriminant characters instead).

targets.target: Residue symbols at 2 and at the infinite places (local Hilbert symbols at 2 and ∞)
targets.note: The dyadic supplementary characters χ₄, χ₈, the sign homomorphism Kˣ → ∏_{real v} {±1} and Br(ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2 exist. Missing: the Hilbert (norm-residue) symbol at 2 or at a real place and the product formula tying the local symbols together.

targets.target: Higher reciprocity through class field theory (cubic, quartic, Eisenstein, general power and Artin reciprocity), with ramified primes excluded
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Artin symbol at unramified primes, the ideal-theoretic Artin map away from S (its kernel and image are not determined), class formations without a reciprocity map, and the Artin map of the genus field of a quadratic field. No cubic, quartic, Eisenstein or general Artin reciprocity law is proved.

duplicates.note: FF.1 constructs Gauss and Jacobi sums over finite fields with their norm and product identities, the same targets as this layer's Gauss/Jacobi item.

Layer 14 defines the local Hilbert invariants at finite and real places, proves the Hilbert product formula and derives quadratic reciprocity including the real and dyadic factors — the 'residue symbols at 2 and at infinite places' target — and names higher power reciprocity as follow-on work.
Layer 11 constructs the global Artin map and its reciprocity law (triviality on principal ideles), the class-field-theory input CA.1 cites for higher reciprocity.
6C owns the {±1}-valued Hilbert symbol over nonarchimedean local fields (dyadic case included) and its product formula.
T.7 compares the norm-residue symbol with the Hilbert symbol and proves the change-of-root rule and global reciprocity for these symbols.

targets.target: Linear recurrences, their relation to companion matrices and eigenvalues (without extending scalars)
targets.note: Mathlib has the solution space of a linear recurrence (≃ initial values), its characteristic polynomial and the geometric solutions from its roots; companion matrices exist only in rank 2 (Tau Ceti). Missing: closed forms with repeated roots, the general companion matrix with charpoly = the recurrence polynomial, and the state-vector/eigenvalue relation.

targets.target: Divisibility sequences: Fibonacci strong divisibility, Lucas sequences U_n(P,Q), elliptic divisibility sequences
targets.note: Fibonacci is a strong divisibility sequence (Mathlib) and Tau Ceti proves Mathlib's TODO that `normEDS b c d` is an elliptic net and a divisibility sequence over any commutative ring. Missing: general Lucas sequences and their strong divisibility, and strong divisibility of EDS.

targets.target: Bernoulli numbers and Euler numbers
targets.note: Bernoulli numbers are complete (both sign conventions, formal generating function over ℚ-algebras, Faulhaber, von Staudt–Clausen, Bernoulli polynomials). Euler numbers (secant/zigzag numbers) are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Binomial identities (Vandermonde, Lucas, Kummer)
targets.note: Vandermonde (also in binomial rings), Lucas's theorem (alias `Choose.lucas_theorem`), Kummer's carry formula for v_p of a binomial coefficient and the binomial theorem in commutative semirings.

targets.target: Rational and formal generating functions (rational power series; generating function of a linear recurrence)
targets.note: Formal power series with inverses, (1−X)^{−d} expansions, the partition product and Catalan functional equation exist, and rational functions embed in Laurent series. Missing: a rationality predicate for power series and the theorem that a sequence satisfies a linear recurrence iff its generating function is P/Q with Q the reversed characteristic polynomial.

targets.target: Radix expansions (integers, reals, p-adics)
targets.note: Base-b digits of naturals with uniqueness and digit-sum congruences, and base-b expansions of reals in [0,1) (existence, no uniqueness statement). p-adic digit expansions ℤ_p ≃ (ℕ → Fin p) are absent.

targets.target: Automatic sequences (k-automatic sequences, automata with output)
targets.note: Only acceptor DFAs exist; there are no automata with output, k-kernels, Thue–Morse or Cobham's theorem in either library.

targets.target: Farey sequences (mediants, neighbour property)
targets.note: Nothing named Farey, mediant, Stern–Brocot or Ford circle; the nearest statement is the determinant identity for consecutive continued-fraction convergents.

targets.target: Combinatorial number families (Catalan, Stirling, Bell, partition numbers, derangements)
targets.note: All named families are defined with their basic closed forms or recursions (Catalan = central binomial/(n+1), Stirling numbers of both kinds, Bell numbers, partition generating function, derangement counts).

targets.target: Christol's theorem (algebraic power series over F_q ↔ p-automatic coefficients)
targets.note: Searched Christol, automatic, and algebraicity of power series over finite fields: nothing in either library.

targets.target: Analytic specializations of formal identities with separate convergence theorems
targets.note: Binet's formula, ζ(2k) and ζ(−n) via Bernoulli numbers, the derangement limit and (Tau Ceti) the convergent Hermite generating function exist. Missing: the convergent Bernoulli generating function z/(e^z−1) for |z| < 2π and a general formal-to-analytic transfer theorem.

duplicates.note: QM.0 builds partition functions, generating products and q-binomial identities in formal power-series rings with separate convergence theorems — the same formal-generating-function and number-family targets.
L0 constructs (generalized) Bernoulli numbers and applies the Mellin argument to the Bernoulli generating function, overlapping the Bernoulli-number and analytic-specialization targets.

targets.target: Integer-valued polynomials (binomial-coefficient basis, Int(ℤ), Pólya's theorem)
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves that the (X choose n) form a basis of K[X] over any ℚ-algebra and a ℤ-basis of their span (closed under multiplication, `TauCeti.mul_mem_ringChooseSpan`), plus integral Newton interpolation; Mathlib has binomial rings and Mahler's basis for C(ℤ_p). Missing: the ring Int(ℤ) itself and Pólya's theorem identifying it with that ℤ-span (a TODO in Mathlib's `Binomial.lean`), and Int(𝓞_K).

targets.target: Irreducibility criteria
targets.note: Eisenstein (prime ideals of domains), Gauss's lemma, the rational root theorem, irreducibility of cyclotomic polynomials over ℚ (and over number fields unramified at q in Tau Ceti), Selmer's X^n−X−1 and Capelli for X^n−a when n is prime, odd, or p^k with p ≠ 2. Not present: Capelli's criterion when 4 | n, and the Perron, Cohn and Newton-polygon criteria.

targets.target: Resultants
targets.note: Sylvester-matrix resultant with the root-product formula for split polynomials, vanishing over a field iff not coprime, the Bézout-type identity and multiplicativity; Tau Ceti identifies the norm in AdjoinRoot g with Res(g,p). Resultants of binary forms are a Mathlib TODO.

targets.target: Discriminants of polynomials
targets.note: Res(f,f′) = ±lc·disc (Mathlib); the root-difference formula over any commutative ring, disc(fg) = disc f·disc g·Res(f,g)², separability over a field iff disc ≠ 0, and reduction mod p separable iff p ∤ disc (Tau Ceti). Trinomial discriminant formulas are absent.

targets.target: Smith normal form with invertible change-of-basis matrices, the reconstruction equation and d_i | d_{i+1}
targets.note: Tau Ceti: for A ∈ M_n(ℤ) with det A ≠ 0 there are L, R ∈ GL_n(ℤ) with LAR = diag(d), d_i | d_j, unique. Mathlib: basis-level Smith form of a submodule of a free module over a PID, without the divisibility chain. Missing: rectangular or singular matrices, general PIDs, and any algorithm with termination.

targets.target: Hermite normal form over ℤ
targets.note: Only HNF-shaped coset representatives for Hecke double cosets, row-echelon predicates and Gauss–Jordan elimination over division rings; no existence or uniqueness of Hermite normal form over ℤ.

targets.target: Rational canonical form and invariant factors (of endomorphisms and of finitely generated modules over a PID)
targets.note: The structure theorem is present in elementary-divisor form R^n × ⊕ R/(p_i^{e_i}); rational canonical form exists only for non-scalar 2×2 matrices over a field (Tau Ceti), and invariant factors only for Gram matrices of integral lattices. Missing: the invariant-factor form d_1 | d_2 | … and the rational canonical form in general.

targets.target: Effective ideal arithmetic (ideal bases via HNF, terminating normal-form algorithms)
targets.note: The ideal norm as |det| of a basis change and an existential multivariate division theorem exist; there is no algorithm computing ideal bases, no Gröbner-basis algorithm and no terminating normal-form procedure.

duplicates.note: Layer 3 states the root-product formula for the discriminant, disc(fg) with its resultant cross term, base change and separability — the resultant/discriminant targets here.
Layer 2 uses Smith normal form with explicit invariant factors and divisibility chain for Gram matrices, overlapping the Smith-normal-form and invariant-factor targets.
CN.1 factors polynomials with checked factors and irreducibility proofs, overlapping the irreducibility/effective-arithmetic side of CA.3.
FF.3 proves finite-field polynomial factorization with checked irreducibility witnesses.
GN.5 supplies reductions with exact change-of-basis certificates, the same certificate contract as CA.3's normal-form algorithms.

targets.target: Pell equations: nontrivial solutions, fundamental solution, classification of all solutions through units with positivity conventions
targets.note: For d > 0 not a square, solutions of x² − dy² = 1 form the unitary group of ℤ√d, a fundamental solution exists, and every solution is ±a₁ⁿ with a unique positive generator. The negative and generalized Pell equations x² − dy² = −1, N and the continued-fraction algorithm are not classified.

targets.target: Sums of squares: two squares, three squares, four squares, representation counts
targets.note: Fermat's two-square theorem with the full characterization of sums of two squares, and Lagrange's four-square theorem. Legendre's three-square theorem and Jacobi's representation counts r₂, r₄ are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Elementary descent: x⁴ + y⁴ = z², Fermat for n = 3, 4, Pythagorean triples
targets.note: Infinite descent for x⁴ + y⁴ = z², FLT for exponents 3 and 4 (`fermatLastTheoremThree` is a `public theorem`, missing from the index) and the classification of Pythagorean triples.

targets.target: Source-scoped exponential Diophantine equations (Catalan–Mihăilescu, Ramanujan–Nagell, 2^a − 3^b = ±1, …)
targets.note: Only tools: the lifting-the-exponent lemma and the polynomial (Mason–Stothers) analogue of Catalan/FLT. No exponential equation over ℤ is solved.

targets.target: Routing of genus-one and higher-genus equations to rational-point owners, preserving primitivity and local solubility
targets.note: An interface rather than a theorem; on the receiving side Tau Ceti already has Mordell–Weil for elliptic curves over number fields and Lutz–Nagell, but no curve-to-equation transfer preserving primitive or local-solubility conditions exists.

targets.target: Linear Diophantine equations and systems
targets.note: Solvability of ax + by = n (over ℤ and Bézout domains) and nonnegative solvability beyond (p−1)(q−1) are proved. The parametrization of all solutions and integer linear systems Ax = b (via Smith form) are absent.

targets.target: Numerical semigroups and Frobenius numbers
targets.note: The Frobenius number of coprime m, n > 1 is mn − m − n, and a Frobenius number exists iff the generators have gcd 1 (and 1 is not a generator). Numerical-semigroup theory (genus, Sylvester's gap count (a−1)(b−1)/2, Apéry sets, symmetry) is absent.

targets.target: Egyptian-fraction identities with precise finite or asymptotic claims
targets.note: Searched Egyptian, unit fraction, Erdős–Straus, Fibonacci–Sylvester and greedy expansions: nothing in either library.

duplicates.note: DT.4 turns logarithmic-form bounds into explicit bounds for Thue, S-unit and exponential equations, the 'source-scoped exponential equations' target.

ED.2 combines those bounds with lattice reduction and certified residual enumeration, matching the 'finite search complete only after a proven bound' acceptance rule for exponential and S-unit equations.
ED.3 owns descent and saturation for genus-one curves, the receiving end of CA.4's routing of genus-one equations.

targets.target: Reuse of integral bases of rings of integers
targets.note: An integral basis exists for every number field (Mathlib), 𝓞 of ℚ(ζ_n) is ℤ[ζ_n] (Mathlib), and 𝓞 of ℚ(√d) is ℤ[√d] or ℤ[(1+√d)/2] for squarefree d (Tau Ceti); nothing to construct here.

targets.target: Reuse of unit groups (Dirichlet's unit theorem, regulator)
targets.note: Dirichlet's unit theorem in unique-decomposition form (Mathlib) and as (𝓞_F)ˣ ≃* torsion × ℤ^rank (Tau Ceti), with the regulator; explicit fundamental units of real quadratic fields are not computed.

targets.target: Reuse of class groups (finiteness, class number, Minkowski bound, explicit class numbers)
targets.note: Finiteness of the class group, the Minkowski bound, h(ℚ(√−5)) = 2 and h(ℚ(√−21)) = 4, class number one for ℚ(ζ₃), ℚ(ζ₅) (`IsCyclotomicExtension.Rat.three_pid`, `five_pid`) and an effective bound h ≤ |d|·4^n.

targets.target: Reuse of relative discriminants and the different
targets.note: The different with its tower formula and ramification criterion (Mathlib) and the relative discriminant ideal N(𝔇_{B/A}) with its tower law and ramification criterion (Tau Ceti). The conductor–discriminant formula is absent.

targets.target: Reuse of Frobenius elements
targets.note: Arithmetic Frobenius elements for invariant extensions of rings with existence and uniqueness at unramified primes (Mathlib), the Artin symbol as a conjugacy class, and the cyclotomic normalization Frob ↦ N𝔭 (Tau Ceti).

targets.target: Reuse of ideal factorization (Dedekind–Kummer; splitting in quadratic and cyclotomic fields)
targets.note: Dedekind–Kummer with inertia and ramification indices, ∑ e f = n, prime splitting in ℚ(ζ_n) (Mathlib) and the quadratic splitting law via the Legendre symbol (Tau Ceti).

targets.target: Connection of certified matrix computations to intrinsic invariants, checked on quadratic and cyclotomic examples
targets.note: The quadratic and cyclotomic discriminants and several class numbers are proved as theorems, so the named comparisons are available. There is no certification pipeline from matrix or LMFDB computations to these invariants; that is ComputationalNumberTheory CN.2's certification scope.

duplicates.note: CN.2 certifies integral bases, orders, ideal decomposition and unit/class groups, the same 'certified computation ↔ intrinsic invariant' connection as CA.5.
Layer 3 owns the power-basis index, the discriminant comparison and Dedekind–Kummer factorization reused here.
Layer 4 defines the relative discriminant ideal (now `TauCeti.relDiscr`) that CA.5 lists among the reused invariants.
Layer 7 owns integral bases of quadratic/cyclotomic fields, monogenicity and explicit units — CA.5's quadratic and cyclotomic acceptance examples.
Layer 2 owns Frobenius elements and the Artin symbol reused by CA.5.

targets.target: Mahler measure of polynomials and of algebraic numbers, with multiplicativity and the root (Jensen) formula
targets.note: For complex polynomials: definition as a circle average, multiplicativity, M(p) = |lc|∏max(1,|α|) and coefficient bounds. The Mahler measure of an algebraic number (of its minimal polynomial over ℤ) is not defined.

targets.target: House of an algebraic number
targets.note: Maximum absolute value over all complex embeddings of an element of a number field, with submultiplicativity and the triangle inequality.

targets.target: Pisot and Salem numbers (certified classification by conjugate moduli)
targets.note: Searched Pisot and Salem (matches are only Salem–Spencer sets): nothing in either library.

targets.target: Dynamical and height comparisons (M(α) versus the Weil height; canonical heights)
targets.note: The absolute Weil height exists (Mathlib) and Tau Ceti has the Néron–Tate canonical height with its bounded difference from the naive height. Missing: log M(α) = deg(α)·h(α) and canonical heights of general polarized dynamical systems.

targets.target: Selected proven lower bounds (Kronecker; Smyth, Dobrowolski, Schinzel–Zassenhaus), with Lehmer kept conjectural
targets.note: Kronecker's theorem is present in polynomial form (M(p) = 1 for p ∈ ℤ[X] forces roots of unity) and for algebraic integers with all conjugates in the unit disc. Smyth's, Dobrowolski's and Schinzel–Zassenhaus bounds are absent.

targets.target: Finiteness statements (Northcott-type: bounded degree and Mahler measure/house)
targets.note: Finitely many integer polynomials of degree ≤ n and Mahler measure ≤ B (with an explicit count), finitely many algebraic integers of a fixed field with bounded house, and Northcott for the Weil height.

targets.target: Distinguishing roots of unity among algebraic integers and algebraic numbers
targets.note: An algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1 is a root of unity, and torsion units are exactly those of house 1.

duplicates.note: DT.0 defines Weil heights with the product-formula normalization, the height side of CA.6's comparisons.
DY.1 constructs canonical heights of polarized morphisms (and CA.6 lists DY.1 as an input for its 'dynamical/height comparisons').
DY.6 keeps dynamical Lehmer conjectural and registers proven cases, the same boundary CA.6 draws for Lehmer-type lower bounds.

targets.target: Rings of integers as modules over group rings (𝓞_L over ℤ[G] or 𝓞_K[G])
targets.note: The Galois action on 𝓞_L exists (Mathlib's `MulSemiringAction G (𝓞 K)` and `IsGaloisGroup G (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L)` instances; Tau Ceti's commuting-action instance), but no group-ring module structure or theory is built on it.

targets.target: Normal basis theorem and normal-basis maps (rational)
targets.note: Every finite Galois extension of an arbitrary field has a basis that is a single Galois orbit (`public noncomputable def`, missing from the index). The K[G]-module isomorphism L ≅ K[G] is not stated, and there is no integral version.

targets.target: Locally free class groups of group rings and orders
targets.note: Only the Picard group of a commutative ring (and its identification with the ideal class group of a domain) exists; locally free class groups of noncommutative orders such as ℤ[G] are absent.

targets.target: Relative resolvent and discriminant data
targets.note: The relative discriminant ideal and different are present; Galois (Lagrange) resolvents in Fröhlich's sense are absent (Tau Ceti's `MvPolynomial.universalResolvent` is a Stauduhar resolvent for computing Galois groups, not this object).

targets.target: Noether's theorem: tame ramification ⇔ 𝓞_L locally free over 𝓞_K[G] (local normal integral bases)
targets.note: Only tame-ramification infrastructure (the tame half of Dedekind's different theorem) exists; no normal integral basis or local freeness statement.

targets.target: Hilbert–Speiser theorem (tame abelian extensions of ℚ have normal integral bases)
targets.note: Searched Hilbert–Speiser, Speiser, normal integral basis: nothing in either library.

targets.target: Fröhlich–Taylor Galois-module class-group theorems and integral representation theorems
targets.note: Searched Fröhlich, Taylor, Galois module, associated order, Swan module: only bibliographic citations of Cassels–Fröhlich.

targets.target: K₀ of rings, imported from existing owners
targets.note: Tau Ceti has split and exact K₀ of categories with the exact structure on finitely generated projective modules, giving K₀(R), and the Cartan map to G₀; Mathlib only has the Grothendieck group of a commutative monoid.

targets.target: Orders in semisimple algebras (ℤ-orders in group algebras, maximal orders)
targets.note: Searched maximal order, hereditary order, ℤ-order: nothing; the nearest object is the index of ℤ[θ] in 𝓞_K.

duplicates.note: Z.1 owns K₀ of rings via finitely generated projectives, which CA.7 says it imports.
Z.4 classifies finite projectives over Dedekind domains (Steinitz), the commutative base case of local-versus-global freeness of 𝓞_L.
FF.0 builds normal bases of finite-field extensions, the finite-field case of CA.7's normal-basis maps.

AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons.summary: The libraries contain only foundations for this roadmap: Mathlib's classical adic completion and regular sequences, the small étale and pro-étale sites of a scheme with a definition of pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology, the limit lemmas for qcqs schemes with affine transition maps (nonemptiness, affineness at a stage, factorization of maps to schemes locally of finite presentation), scheme-theoretic images, relative normalization and generic smoothness over perfect fields; Tau Ceti adds Spa of Huber pairs and the packaging of models and numerical types for stable reduction. Genuinely missing: derived completeness, adic coefficient categories and ∞-categorical presentability; v-sheaves, diamonds and marked untilts; absolute noetherian approximation, Nagata compactification, scheme Rf_! and topological invariance of the étale site; blowups, de Jong's alterations, cohomological descent and local purity; and every ECD 27 comparison theorem.

targets.target: Derived I-completeness and the derived completion functor for an I-adically complete coefficient ring Λ with I generated by a regular sequence
targets.note: Mathlib has only classical I-adic completeness and completion of modules (complete when I is finitely generated), regular and weakly regular sequences, and algebraic local cohomology as colim Ext(R/Jᵗ, M). There is no derived-complete object in any derived category, no derived completion functor and no Koszul-complex model.

targets.target: D_ét(X,Λ) for adic Λ: derived I-complete objects of the v-derived category that are étale after derived reduction mod I, distinguished from D_ét of Λ as a discrete ring
targets.note: Only the derived category of an abelian category, sheaf cohomology as Ext on a site and Grothendieck-abelianness of sheaves on the small étale site of a scheme exist. v-sheaves, diamonds and D_ét with any coefficients are absent from both libraries.

targets.target: ECD Proposition 26.2 at the enhanced level: presentability and stability, and equivalence with the limit of the categories for Λ/Iⁿ
targets.note: Mathlib has locally presentable 1-categories and the definition of quasicategories, but no stable or presentable ∞-categories and no limit-of-categories reconstruction.

targets.target: Completed tensor product and completed colimits, with the failure of the uncompleted inclusion to preserve them
targets.note: Only module-level statements: R̂ ⊗_R M ≃ M̂ for R noetherian and M finite, flatness of R̂, and base change of restricted power series over complete noetherian Tate rings. No completed tensor product of complexes or sheaves.

targets.target: Six operations for the adic coefficient system with finite-level compatibility, regular-sequence dévissage for right adjoints and internal Hom, and detection of equivalences modulo I
targets.note: Nakayama-type detection exists for finitely generated modules only (I ⊆ Jacobson radical of an I-adically complete ring). No étale, diamond or adic six-functor formalism exists.

targets.target: Adic forms of the basic theorems for Λ = ℤ_ℓ, I = (ℓ), ℓ ≠ p, and rational ℓ-adic coefficients by a separate localization
targets.note: Mathlib defines Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ) of a scheme only, as pro-étale cohomology of U ↦ C(U, ℤ_ℓ), with no theorems and no comparison with lim Hⁿ(X, ℤ/ℓⁿ); there are no ℚ_ℓ-coefficient categories and nothing for diamonds.

duplicates.note: E4 extends derived adic completion to sheaves and compatible coefficient systems, proves the reconstruction from the categories with coefficients Λ/Iⁿ under the same regular-sequence hypotheses and supplies completed tensor products and colimits; it says L0 only applies this to étale objects.
DD.1 constructs derived I-completeness, the derived completion functor, completed tensor products and completed colimits, the generic module-level targets underlying L0.
C2 defines D_ét for diamonds and proves its presentability and stability, the discrete-coefficient version of the category L0 completes.

targets.target: The small v-sheaf of a characteristic-p scheme via Spa(A, integral closure of F_p in A), independent of the affine cover, functorial and factoring through perfection
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines Spa(A, A⁺) as a set of continuous valuations bounded by 1 on A⁺ and proves it is unchanged when A⁺ is replaced by its integral closure; Mathlib has the perfection of rings with its universal property. There is no v-topology, no v-sheaf or diamond, no gluing of Spa over a scheme and no perfection of schemes.

targets.target: Étale and pro-étale comparison morphisms of sites between the scheme and its v-sheaf
targets.note: Mathlib has the small étale and small pro-étale sites of a scheme, the inequality of the big étale and pro-étale topologies and pushforward along continuous functors, but no morphism of sites to any v-site or diamond site.

targets.target: Mixed-characteristic version over a complete DVR O with perfect residue field: marked untilts over Spa(O,O) with a map of locally ringed spaces to the scheme, and the relative representability statements of ECD 27.5
targets.note: Mathlib has the multiplicative untilt map PreTilt O p → O for p-adically complete O, Fontaine's θ : W(R♭) → R and the abstract notion of a relatively representable functor. Marked untilts as a v-sheaf and the representability statements are absent.

targets.target: Comparison maps between the (k,k) convention and the (k, integral closure of F_p) convention at a residue field, where such maps exist
targets.note: A discrete ring with A⁺ = A is a Huber pair, every valuation on a discrete ring is continuous, and enlarging the plus ring shrinks Spa (so Spa(k,k) ⊆ Spa(k, F̄_p ∩ k) as sets). No comparison of the associated v-sheaves or adic spaces is stated.

duplicates.note: D6 constructs Spd ℤ_p and Spd(A,A⁺) by marked untilts, the same marked-untilt construction L1 uses over Spa(O,O), though D6 restricts to Tate pairs and analytic adic spaces rather than schemes.

targets.target: Noetherian approximation: limits of qcqs schemes with affine transition maps
targets.note: For a given limit cone of a cofiltered diagram of quasi-compact (or qcqs) schemes with affine transition maps, Mathlib proves nonemptiness, quasi-compactness, that affineness of the limit descends to a stage (Stacks 01Z2, 01Z6) and that finite affine covers descend. Missing: the existence of such limits in general and absolute noetherian approximation of a qcqs scheme by finite-type ℤ-schemes (Stacks 01ZA).

targets.target: Finite-presentation descent of morphisms and diagrams to a finite stage, with eventual recognition of properties (separated, proper, closed immersion, étale)
targets.note: Morphisms from the limit to a scheme locally of finite presentation factor through a stage, two stage maps that agree on the limit agree later (finite type), and Hom_S(−, X) turns these limits into colimits. Missing: descent of finitely presented schemes and diagrams themselves (Stacks 01ZM) and eventual separatedness, properness, closed immersion or étaleness; only affineness and quasi-affineness are proved eventually.

targets.target: Étale and cohomological continuity under such limits
targets.note: Only global sections commute with these limits; there is no continuity of étale sites or of étale cohomology (Stacks 09YQ).

targets.target: Reduction of a separated finite-type morphism to a closed immersion into a separated finitely presented morphism
targets.note: Searched the limit and finite-presentation files and the index for embeddings of finite-type morphisms into finitely presented ones (Stacks 09ZP): nothing.

targets.target: Scheme-theoretic image and closure
targets.note: The scheme-theoretic image is the closed subscheme cut out by the kernel ideal sheaf, with the factorization of f and its universal property via the ideal-sheaf/kernel adjunction; for quasi-compact f the factor X → image is dominant.

targets.target: Nagata compactification of separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes (nonnoetherian)
targets.note: Searched Nagata, compactification, compactifiable: the only related geometry is Zariski's Main Theorem (proper and locally quasi-finite ⇒ finite; a separated quasi-compact locally quasi-finite morphism locally of finite type is an open immersion into its relative normalization).

targets.target: Compactly supported direct image Rf_! for separated finite-type morphisms of qcqs schemes, by extension by zero and proper pushforward, with independence of compactification, composition, base change and projection formula
targets.note: Only generic pushforward and pullback of sheaves along functors of sites exist; no extension by zero, proper base change or Rf_! for étale sheaves on schemes.

targets.target: Extension from finite coefficient rings by colimit and perfect-complex arguments, and passage to perfections through topological invariance of the étale site
targets.note: Mathlib proves Spec f is a homeomorphism when ker f is nil and every element has a power in the image (Stacks 0BR8), but has no universal homeomorphisms of schemes, no perfection of schemes and no equivalence of étale sites (Stacks 04DY).

duplicates.note: SF.2 owns scheme sheaf cohomology with localization, proper base change and compact support, overlapping L2's construction of the scheme Rf_! and its base-change and projection formulas.

targets.target: Comparison pullback from the scheme étale derived category of a characteristic-p scheme to D_ét of its v-sheaf, and its right adjoint
targets.note: Searched diamond, v-sheaf, comparison functor: nothing beyond the scheme étale site and its points in Mathlib.

targets.target: ECD 27.1–27.3: full faithfulness of the comparison pullback on the specified derived categories (via perfected affine space, algebraically closed nonarchimedean fields, exhaustion by balls and constructibility)
targets.note: No derived category of étale sheaves on diamonds or adic spaces exists in either library.

targets.target: ECD 27.4: for separated finite-type maps of qcqs characteristic-p schemes, compactifiability, representability in locally spatial diamonds, finite dim.trg, the Rf_! comparison and the right-adjoint identity for Rf^!
targets.note: Absent together with its prerequisites (scheme Rf_!, diamond Rf_!, dim.trg).

duplicates.note: EDC.6 proves the scheme/adic/diamond comparisons of operations explicitly through L2–L6, restating L3's Rf_! comparison as its transport target.

targets.target: ECD 27.5: geometric eligibility and the Rf_! comparison for separated finite-type schemes over a complete DVR with perfect residue field, with its right-adjoint consequence
targets.note: No scheme or diamond Rf_! exists in either library.

targets.target: The analytic test space {x ≠ 0} ⊂ Spa O[[x]]: construction, analytic smoothness and conservativity after passing to diamonds
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the analytic locus of Spa, rational subsets and spectrality of Spa given a pair of definition, but no Huber-pair structure on O[[x]] with the (π,x)-adic topology, no adic spaces as sheafy ringed spaces over it and no smoothness.

targets.target: Algebraic/analytic proper base-change comparison with its base-change compatibility
targets.note: Searched proper base change, analytification, GAGA: nothing in either library.

duplicates.note: EDC.6 transports the mixed-characteristic scheme/adic/diamond Rf_! comparison of L4 into its comparison of operations.

targets.target: Normalization of schemes under the applicable excellence hypotheses
targets.note: Mathlib constructs the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property among integral factorizations and compatibility with smooth base change. Missing: finiteness of normalization (no excellent, Nagata or Japanese rings in either library).

targets.target: Blowups, strict transforms and flattening by blowup
targets.note: Only the Rees algebra R[It] exists (its docstring anticipates blowups); searched blowup, blow-up, strict transform, flattening, Raynaud–Gruson in both libraries. Tau Ceti's only blow-up is of plumbing graphs in low-dimensional topology.

targets.target: Generic smoothness
targets.note: A reduced scheme locally of finite presentation over a perfect field has dense (open) smooth locus, the form used over perfect base fields; a relative generic-smoothness theorem for morphisms is not stated.

targets.target: Compactification of pairs and induction on dimension
targets.note: No compactification results for schemes exist (see L2).

targets.target: Curve fibrations, extension of the generic curve with marked boundary, finite base extension and stable or semistable reduction of the family
targets.note: Tau Ceti has flat finitely presented models over a DVR with a fixed generic-fibre isomorphism and the combinatorics of numerical types (Stacks 0C7B, 0C7I), all sorry-free; there are no nodal or semistable curves or families and no stable reduction theorem.

targets.target: de Jong's alteration theorems (Theorems 4.1 and 6.5): smooth alterations with normal-crossing boundary over a field and strictly semistable alterations over a valuation base
targets.note: No hits for alteration or de Jong in either library.

targets.target: Proper hypercovers by alterations and their cohomological descent
targets.note: Mathlib has 1-hypercovers (used for sheaf conditions) and Čech complexes; hypercovers of all degrees, proper or h-topologies and cohomological descent are absent.

targets.target: Local étale purity, Kummer and nearby-cycle calculations for smooth strata and normal-crossing boundaries, with Galois actions and analytic versions
targets.note: Only Kummer theory for fields exists: Kˣ/(Kˣ)ⁿ injects into H¹(G_K, μₙ) for n invertible in K (Tau Ceti; surjectivity is not proved) and Gal(K(ⁿ√a)/K) ≅ μₙ (Mathlib). No étale sheaf R^i j_* or nearby cycles.

duplicates.note: SF.4 owns formal schemes, semistable reduction and alterations, the same de Jong alteration and semistable-reduction targets.

Layer 7 proves semistable (nodal) reduction of curves after finite separable base extension, the curve-family input L5 says it will consume or prove.

R09.7a constructs blowups by the Rees algebra with strict, total and controlled transforms and simple normal-crossing boundaries (in characteristic zero), overlapping L5's blowup and strict-transform geometry.
IG.4 computes R^i j_* along a normal-crossings boundary from exterior powers of local Kummer classes, the same local purity/Kummer calculation as L5's fifth task.
E2 constructs hypercovers and cohomological descent, which L5 needs for proper hypercovers by alterations.

targets.target: ECD 27.6: constructible direct-image comparison for separated finite-type maps over O with finite coefficients killed by an integer prime to p
targets.note: No constructible étale sheaves on schemes or adic spaces exist; the only constructibility result is Chevalley's theorem for sets (`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isConstructible_image`).

targets.target: Explicit Galois-cohomology calculation with the inertia group for Spec K → Spec O (tame inertia ≅ ∏_{ℓ≠p} ℤ_ℓ(1))
targets.note: Inertia subgroups of valuation subrings, |inertia| = e for finite Galois extensions with perfect residue fields and lower ramification groups for places of function fields exist; the tame quotient of absolute inertia, its identification with ∏ ℤ_ℓ(1) and its cohomology are absent.

targets.target: ECD 27.7: constructible full faithfulness for schemes locally of finite type over O with prime-to-p coefficients
targets.note: Absent together with its prerequisites.

duplicates.note: EDC.6 transports L6's constructible comparison and full faithfulness into its scheme/adic/diamond comparison of operations.

ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology.summary: Nothing in either library works on adic spaces beyond Tau Ceti's foundations: Spa of Huber pairs as a topological space, rational subsets, valuation spectra, Tate algebras and microbial valuations. Mathlib supplies the general sheaf theory these stages would build on — points of sites and conservative families, the small étale site of a scheme with its geometric points, enough injectives and right derived functors on D⁺, sheaf cohomology as Ext with Mayer–Vietoris (and a long exact sequence in Tau Ceti) — together with henselian pairs and inertia and decomposition subgroups of valuation subrings. Genuinely missing: the étale site and étale cohomology of adic spaces, constructible sheaves and supports, strict henselization, formal schemes and Huber's specialization and formal comparison theorems, nearby cycles over valuation bases and pro-p wild inertia, proper support, trace and Poincaré duality for curves, cohomology of discs and annuli, analytification with its comparison theorems, and Lütkebohmert's compactification.

targets.target: The étale site of analytic adic spaces and sheaves of Λ-modules on it
targets.note: Mathlib's small étale site is for schemes only; Tau Ceti has Spa(A,A⁺) as a topological space and a presentation-indexed presheaf that its docstring says is not yet the structure sheaf. There are no adic spaces as objects, no étale morphisms of adic spaces and no étale site.

targets.target: Injective resolutions, D⁺, derived global sections and derived direct image for sheaves on a site
targets.note: Sheaf categories on essentially small sites are Grothendieck abelian with enough injectives, every additive functor between abelian categories with enough injectives has a total right derived functor on D⁺ (its triangulated structure is a TODO), and sheaf cohomology is defined as Ext from the constant sheaf ℤ. Missing: RΓ and Rf_* as functors on D⁺ of sheaves and the identification of Sheaf.H with R^nΓ.

targets.target: Torsion local systems, constructible sheaves in the analytic sense, Tate twists and supports (extension by zero, sections with support)
targets.note: Only constant sheaves, the sheafified free abelian sheaf ℤ_U on a representable (Hom(ℤ_U, F) = F(U)) and μₙ(K^sep) as a Galois module exist. No locally constant or constructible Λ-sheaves, μₙ^{⊗r} sheaves, j_!, i^! or Γ_Z.

targets.target: Geometric points Spa(C,C⁺) → X and geometric stalks, the stalk formula over strict localization and affine-local descriptions
targets.note: Mathlib has points of sites as fibre functors with stalks, conservative families of points, the stalk of a point built from a cofiltered diagram as a colimit over it, and geometric points of the small étale site of a scheme forming a conservative family. Missing: strict localization and the formula F_x̄ = Γ(Spec O^sh, F), and any points or stalks for adic spaces with field pairs (C,C⁺).

targets.target: Leray spectral sequence and Čech-to-derived comparison
targets.note: The long exact cohomology sequence of a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves (Tau Ceti), the Mayer–Vietoris sequence, the Čech complex of a family and spectral sequences of spectral objects exist, but no Leray or Grothendieck spectral sequence is constructed and the Čech complex is not compared with sheaf cohomology.

targets.target: Continuity of cohomology under the cofiltered limits used in the classical proofs, distinguishing adic inverse limits from Huber tilde-limits
targets.note: Only AB5 for sheaf categories and the degree-one continuous group cohomology colimit over finite quotients exist; no limits of sites or topoi and no colimit formula for cohomology of a limit space.

E1 constructs module sheaves on sites with injective resolutions and derived pushforward/pullback, overlapping H0's derived-functor targets (in the enhanced setting).

targets.target: Formal schemes of type (S), their adic spaces d(X), the specialization morphism λ_X : d(X)_ét → X_ét and the identification of X_ét with the étale topos of the reduced special scheme

No formal schemes (no Spf), no adic spaces as ringed spaces, no specialization map and no topological invariance of étale sites.

targets.target: Hub96 3.5.16 over a microbial valuation ring and the identification 3.5.17 with the trait nearby-cycle object RΨ, with its inertia action
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines microbial valuations (a convex subgroup with nontrivial archimedean quotient, Wedhorn 5.46) and proves continuous analytic points of Spa are microbial; the pseudo-adic comparison and any nearby-cycle object are absent.

targets.target: Nearby cycles RΨ_L(F) = i*Rj_*j*F over spectra of valuation rings, with Galois action, base-change maps and independence of choices (Hub96 4.2.3)
targets.note: Searched nearby cycles, vanishing cycles, RΨ: nothing; there are no étale sheaves on schemes over valuation rings to apply i*, Rj_* and j* to.

targets.note: Searched nearby cycles, vanishing cycles, RΨ: nothing; there are no étale sheaves on schemes over valuation rings to apply i*, Rj_* and j* to.

DeligneWeightsAndPurity.summary: The libraries contain the linear algebra and some analytic and Hodge-theoretic analogues this roadmap would use, but none of its ℓ-adic mathematics: Mathlib has characteristic polynomials, generalized eigenspace decompositions and perfect pairings, and Tau Ceti adds Landau's theorem for nonnegative Dirichlet series, the 3-4-1 positivity inequality for Euler factors, sl₂ decompositions, symplectic cap invariance, mixed Hodge structures with strictness, and elliptic-curve point-count infrastructure (deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q), a conditional Hasse bound). Genuinely missing: Weil numbers and weights, Frobenius on abelian varieties, the Rosati involution and Tate modules, the Hasse and Weil bounds, Lefschetz pencils, Chebotarev for function fields, lisse and mixed sheaves, monodromy filtrations and quasi-unipotence, Künneth, Leray and weak Lefschetz, every Weil I and Weil II theorem, geometric semisimplicity and hard Lefschetz.

targets.target: Weil q-numbers of integer weight (every complex conjugate of absolute value q^{w/2}) with products, inverses and duals, powers, Tate twists, change q → qⁿ and uniqueness of the weight for q > 1; integrality kept separate
targets.note: Searched Weil number, q-Weil, pure of weight: nothing. Related: Kronecker's theorem (an algebraic integer all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1 is a root of unity, i.e. weight 0), the house of an algebraic number, and σ(aⁿ) = σ(a)ⁿ over an algebraically closed field.

targets.target: ι-weights of nonzero elements of the coefficient field via an isomorphism ι : Q̄_ℓ ≅ ℂ, with real weights
targets.note: Mathlib proves two uncountable algebraically closed fields of characteristic 0 of the same cardinality are isomorphic and defines the algebraic closure of ℚ_p, but not #Q̄_ℓ = 𝔠, a chosen ι, or any ι-weight.

targets.target: Weights of an invertible endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space, defined through the roots of its characteristic polynomial over a splitting field using generalized eigenspaces rather than an eigenbasis, with explicit Jordan-block examples
targets.note: The linear algebra the definition rests on (a declared dependency of the layer) is in Mathlib: eigenvalues are the roots of the characteristic polynomial, over an algebraically closed field the maximal generalized eigenspaces span V with dimensions equal to root multiplicities, and the characteristic polynomial commutes with base change. Missing: the weight predicate on endomorphisms itself, which needs the absent Weil-number and ι-weight notions.

targets.target: Preservation of weights under invariant subspaces, quotients and extensions, via multiplicativity of the characteristic polynomial
targets.note: Mathlib has det e = det(e|W)·det(e on V/W) for an invariant submodule with free W and V/W, the characteristic polynomial of a product map and of block-triangular matrices, and eigenvectors of a restriction. Missing: charpoly(e) = charpoly(e|W)·charpoly(e on V/W) and the resulting statement on eigenvalue sets of subobjects, quotients and extensions.

targets.target: Spectra of tensor products and duals of endomorphisms
targets.note: Determinants of Kronecker products, traces of tensor products, the determinant of the dual map and the characteristic polynomial of a transpose are proved. Missing: the eigenvalues (with multiplicity) of f ⊗ g as products αβ and the characteristic polynomial of the dual map as an endomorphism.

targets.target: Reciprocal pairing of eigenvalues α ↔ c/α induced by a Frobenius-equivariant perfect pairing ⟨Fx,Fy⟩ = c⟨x,y⟩
targets.note: Mathlib expresses charpoly(A⁻¹) through the reversed characteristic polynomial and has perfect pairings; Tau Ceti proves AᵀJA = d·J implies det A = d in rank 2 only. The general similitude statement (spectrum stable under α ↦ c/α with multiplicities) is absent.

targets.target: Distinct pure weights give disjoint eigenvalue sets and hence no nonzero Frobenius-equivariant map
targets.note: An intertwiner maps each generalized eigenspace of f into the one of g with the same eigenvalue, and generalized eigenspaces for distinct eigenvalues are disjoint; the corollary Hom(V,W)^F = 0 for disjoint spectra is not stated.

duplicates.note: R34.1 restates DWP.0's Weil numbers, chosen-embedding versus algebraic weights and tensor/dual/twist rules as imports, with a representation-convention adapter.

WC.2 derives invertibility of F and the reciprocal eigenvalue pairing and polynomial reciprocity from the Frobenius-equivariant Poincaré pairing, the same linear algebra as DWP.0's reciprocal-pairing target.

targets.target: Frobenius and Verschiebung of a polarized abelian variety over a finite field compared under the Rosati involution, with π†π = [q]
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines abelian varieties (proper geometrically integral group schemes), their endomorphism rings and the q-power Frobenius isogeny of a Weierstrass curve over a finite field. Frobenius of abelian varieties, Verschiebung, dual isogenies, polarizations and the Rosati involution are absent.

targets.target: Weil's Riemann hypothesis for abelian varieties: via Rosati positivity, every complex embedding of a Frobenius eigenvalue on the Tate realization has absolute value √q, with the characteristic polynomial of Frobenius
targets.note: Only a conditional matrix form of the Hasse bound (t² ≤ 4q if det(r·M − s·1) is congruent to a nonnegative integer for a 2×2 matrix with det M = q and det(1 − M) = q + 1 − t; the Weil-pairing input is not supplied) and the local L-polynomial 1 − aT + qT² of an elliptic curve over a DVR exist.

targets.target: Tate modules and the identification of H¹ of a smooth proper geometrically connected curve with the Tate realization of its Jacobian (Abel–Jacobi/Picard), with explicit H¹ and geometric-Frobenius normalization
targets.note: Mathlib only defines pro-étale Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ); Tau Ceti identifies the points of an elliptic curve with Cl⁰ of its function field and proves #ker[n] = n² over an algebraically closed field with n invertible. No Tate module, Jacobian variety or H¹ comparison.

targets.target: H⁰/H² weights, the Weil bound |#C(F_{qⁿ}) − qⁿ − 1| ≤ 2g q^{n/2} for all n, and compatibility with finite base extension, including disconnected curves via components and permutation Frobenius
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Riemann–Roch for function fields, finiteness of the degree-zero class group over a finite constant field, the Frobenius trace a_q = q + 1 − #E(F_q) and deg(1 − π_q) = #E(F_q); the Hasse bound itself, zeta functions of curves and the Weil bound are absent.

duplicates.note: R34.2 restates DWP.1's curve/abelian Weil bound with the H¹/Jacobian comparison and Rosati positivity as imports.

Layer 3 proves the Hasse bound, the genus-one case of DWP.1's point-count bound.
WC.5 derives |N_r − (q^r + 1)| ≤ 2g q^{r/2} for curves from b₁ = 2g via the curve/Jacobian cohomology supplier, the same point-count target.

targets.target: Point-count error bounds after identifying degree-zero, top-degree and component contributions
targets.note: Only elliptic-curve point-count infrastructure exists; no general bounds.

targets.target: Exact weight/monodromy statements for LPV's invariant-cycle and semistable-curve applications (equal-characteristic curve-local monodromy purity, semistable-curve weight calculations)
targets.note: Only the combinatorics of special fibres (numerical types) exist; no monodromy or weights.

targets.target: Acceptance examples: ℙⁿ, a curve and its Jacobian, conjugate weights of a quadratic Weil number, ℚ_ℓ(1) of weight −2, nonsemisimple Frobenius, G_m with ordinary and compact-support weights, a nodal degeneration and a smooth proper nonprojective variety
targets.note: Only the Hodge analogue of the Tate twist (ℤ(m) of weight −2m) exists.

duplicates.note: R34.6 consumes DWP.10's export contracts for eigenform/Kuga–Sato purity and coefficient-independent bounds.

targets.target: Weil I Theorem 3.2: a lisse ℚ_ℓ-sheaf on an open of ℙ¹ with a nondegenerate alternating pairing to ℚ_ℓ(−β), geometric monodromy open in the symplectic group and rational local characteristic polynomials is punctually pure of weight β
targets.note: No lisse sheaves, monodromy groups or local characteristic polynomials exist in either library.

targets.target: The even tensor-power argument: rational nonnegative local trace powers and nonnegative Euler-factor coefficients via logarithmic derivatives
targets.note: Searched tensor power trick and Euler factors of sheaves: nothing.

targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Landau's theorem for ordinary Dirichlet series Σ aₙ n^{−s} with aₙ ≥ 0 (no analytic continuation across a real abscissa of absolute convergence, and a pole for meromorphic continuations); Mathlib proves positivity on ℝ of entire continuations. Pringsheim's theorem for power series in T (the form used for local Euler factors in q^{−s}) is absent.

targets.target: Symplectic invariant theory: invariants and coinvariants of tensor powers of the standard representation of Sp computed by contraction pairings
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the contraction V ⊗ V → k is Sp-invariant and the Brauer generator commutes with Sp on V^{⊗2}. Missing: the first fundamental theorem (invariants of V^{⊗2k} spanned by products of pairings) for general tensor powers.

targets.target: H²_c of the tensor powers via Poincaré duality and location of global poles by the trace formula, giving the bound with error tending to zero and the lower bound from reciprocal eigenvalues
targets.note: No compactly supported cohomology, Poincaré duality or trace formula exists.

targets.target: Corollaries 3.8–3.9: coarse weight intervals for H¹_c(U,F) and H¹(ℙ¹, j_*F), algebraicity from rational local factors, absolute convergence of the Euler product and the boundary exact sequence
targets.note: Only Euler products over primes of absolutely summable multiplicative functions exist; no L-functions of sheaves or Euler products over closed points.

duplicates.note: R34.5 restates DWP.2–4's Weil I majoration, pencil rationality and smooth-projective RH proof as imports.
Layer 8 owns Landau's theorem for nonnegative Dirichlet series with the meromorphic-order corollary, the positive-series/pole lemma DWP.2 lists.
Layer 9 identifies the centralizer of the symplectic group on tensor powers with the Brauer algebra of contraction diagrams, the symplectic invariant theory DWP.2 says it must otherwise supply.

targets.target: For a Lefschetz pencil on an even-dimensional smooth projective variety: the vanishing local system E, its orthogonal E^⊥, the radical E ∩ E^⊥ and the quotient with its alternating pairing, twist and Frobenius/descent compatibility
targets.note: Only the linear algebra exists (orthogonal complements, radicals, dim W + dim W^⊥ = dim V + dim(W ∩ V^⊥) for reflexive forms); no pencils, vanishing cycles or local systems.

targets.target: Weil I Theorem 6.2: rationality of every local characteristic polynomial of the radical quotient
targets.note: Searched rationality of local factors: nothing beyond the reversed characteristic polynomial det(1 − X·M).

targets.target: §6 comparison with geometrically constant factors, finite families of eigenvalues and their powers, product/eigenvalue separation lemmas and exceptional-root exclusions
targets.note: No such statements exist.

targets.target: Function-field Chebotarev density for closed points, with conjugacy classes in finite étale quotients and the degree congruences imposed by the constant-field extension
targets.note: Mathlib has arithmetic Frobenius elements at primes with finite residue field; Tau Ceti has decomposition fields of places of function fields and number-field Chebotarev infrastructure (Frobenius prime sets), but no density theorem for function fields or closed points.

targets.target: Frobenius classes in a closed Haar-measure-zero exceptional set have density zero, and density of Frobenius elements in the compact ℓ-adic monodromy image
targets.note: Only normalized Haar probability on compact groups and nullity of proper subspaces for Lebesgue/Haar measure exist.

targets.target: Corollary 6.3 for H¹ of the quotient's j_* extension, retaining the radical and geometrically constant terms
targets.note: Absent together with the étale cohomology it concerns.

duplicates.note: LPV.4 constructs the vanishing-cycle subspace E, E^⊥ and the nondegenerate pairing on E/(E ∩ E^⊥), the same objects as DWP.3's first target.

targets.note: Mathlib defines spectral sequences abstractly; there is no Leray spectral sequence, blowup or étale cohomology.

targets.target: Descent and extension of the projective embedding, pencil and vanishing cycles after a finite extension, with transfer back by powers of Frobenius
targets.note: No Lefschetz pencils or Frobenius actions on cohomology exist.

targets.target: Künneth for even Cartesian powers and the tensor-power removal of the half-unit error, with the limiting step giving |α| = q^{d/2} for every complex conjugate
targets.note: Searched Künneth and tensor power trick: nothing.

targets.target: Reduction of arbitrary degrees to the middle degree by weak Lefschetz, duality and smooth hyperplane sections, handling components and finite-field descent
targets.note: No weak Lefschetz or Poincaré duality exists.

targets.target: The Riemann hypothesis for smooth projective varieties over finite fields (Weil I 1.6–1.7) exported to WeilConjectures
targets.note: Only specific point counts (#ℙ(V) over F_q) and Chevalley–Warning exist; no zeta function of a variety and no RH statement.

duplicates.note: R34.5 restates DWP.4's smooth-projective RH proof as an import.

WC.3 carries out Weil I (1.7) ⇒ (1.6), the all-conjugates RH handoff that DWP.4 exports.

targets.target: Punctually ι-pure and ι-mixed lisse and constructible sheaves, their finite weight filtrations and weight classes modulo ℤ, with coefficient-embedding and twist reductions for real weights
targets.note: Only the Hodge-theoretic analogue (mixed Hodge structures with rational weight filtration and pure graded pieces) and the definition of pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes exist; no sheaves with Frobenius action or pointwise weights.

targets.target: Local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve: weights of the monodromy graded pieces and of boundary invariants of j_*F, with quasi-unipotent reduction, finite covers, tensor/dual compatibility and the Frobenius–N relation
targets.note: Searched monodromy filtration, Jacobson–Morozov, quasi-unipotent, Weil–Deligne: nothing. Only sl₂-triples, the additive Jordan–Chevalley decomposition and unipotence via the characteristic polynomial exist.

targets.target: Weil II's generalization of the fundamental estimate to ι-real systems, irreducible constituents and compatible pairings, with the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin positivity argument, the strict initial H¹ weight bound, convergence, poles, multiplicities and weight-integrality detection
targets.note: Only the positivity input exists: for 0 ≤ a < 1 and |z| ≤ 1, 0 ≤ 3Re(−log(1−a)) + 4Re(−log(1−az)) + Re(−log(1−az²)), with a version for any nonnegative trigonometric combination (Tau Ceti), and Mathlib's application of the same trick to Dirichlet L-functions on Re s = 1, plus Euler products over primes. Missing: the argument for Euler products with factors det(1 − F·t)⁻¹ of ι-real sheaves, the strict H¹ bound and everything sheaf-theoretic.

duplicates.note: LPV.1 constructs tame inertia, the nilpotent logarithm N, quasi-unipotence and the monodromy filtration that DWP.5's local weight theorem imports and extends.
Layer 8.2 packages the 3-4-1 trigonometric positivity argument, the Hadamard–de la Vallée-Poussin step DWP.5 lists.

targets.target: Weil II 3.2.3: for j : U₀ ↪ C₀ with C₀ smooth proper and F₀ lisse punctually ι-pure of weight w, Hⁱ(C, j_*F) is pure of weight w + i
targets.note: No étale cohomology of curves with coefficients exists.

targets.target: Reduction via finite covers to the tame/unipotent case with trace splitting and the resulting direct-summand statements over ℚ_ℓ
targets.note: Only the group-cohomological shadow exists: corestriction after restriction is multiplication by the index on continuous H¹ (and H², H⁰), and Tr(algebraMap x) = [S:R]·x.

targets.target: The correct duality for j_*F with its boundary comparison
targets.note: No duality for étale sheaves exists.

targets.target: External product on C × C, a general pencil, the coefficient-specific local calculation of Weil II 3.1, Leray for R¹f_* and the δ ↦ δ/2 square-improvement iteration with the dual lower bound
targets.note: None of these constructions exist.

targets.target: Exports: the fixed-ι real-weight theorem, the all-embeddings integer-weight theorem and the boundary monodromy weights
targets.note: Absent together with the purity theorem.

duplicates.note: R34.5 restates DWP.5–8's local and mixed-sheaf proof, including this curve purity step, as an import.

targets.target: Weil II 3.3.1: for separated finite-type f over a finite field and F mixed of weights ≤ w, R^i f_! F is mixed of weights ≤ w + i, with its dévissage and a fixed-ι real-weight version
targets.note: No Rf_!, mixed sheaves or weights exist in either library.

targets.target: Consequences: Hⁱ_c weights ≤ w + i; for smooth X and lisse F of weights ≥ w, Hⁱ weights ≥ w + i by Poincaré duality; purity of the image of Hⁱ_c → Hⁱ; purity for smooth proper X
targets.note: Searched purity, Weil conjectures, Riemann hypothesis for varieties: nothing (Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis concerns ζ).

targets.target: The smooth proper nonprojective extension with constant coefficients (Weil II 3.3.9)
targets.note: Absent.

targets.note: Only Kronecker's theorem on algebraic integers with all conjugates of absolute value 1 is related.

FF.2 imports DWP.7's cohomological weight estimates for exponential-sum bounds.
R34.5 restates DWP.5–8's Rf_! bounds and smooth-proper purity as imports.

targets.target: Mixed complexes on the bounded constructible derived category: weights ≤ w stalkwise, weights ≥ w via the dualizing complex, purity, and the weight w + m − 2r of F[m] ⊗ ℚ_ℓ(r)
targets.note: No constructible derived category or dualizing complex exists; only abstract t-structures.

targets.target: Stability of mixed complexes under the six operations with the directional weight estimates (f*, Rf_! preserve upper weights; f^!, Rf_* lower; duality reverses; tensor adds), and preservation of purity by proper direct image
targets.note: No six-functor formalism exists.

targets.target: Weil II 3.4.1: weight-class decomposition modulo ℤ and the unique functorial strict weight filtration on lisse mixed sheaves with integral weights
targets.note: Only analogues exist: strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures for the weight filtration (Tau Ceti), strict morphisms of filtered objects and independence of generalized eigenspaces (Mathlib). No filtration by absolute values of Frobenius eigenvalues and no uniqueness statement.

targets.target: Geometric semisimplicity of punctually ι-pure lisse sheaves on a normal base, via the Ext¹/Hochschild–Serre comparison and the H¹ lower bound
targets.note: Inflation–restriction exactness on H¹ (continuous in Tau Ceti, discrete in Mathlib), Clifford's theorem that restrictions of irreducibles to normal subgroups are semisimple, and semisimplicity of polarizable Hodge structures exist. EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves.summary: Mathlib provides general foundations only: t-structures with truncation triangles, the heart as a subcategory property, BBD's criterion for abelian subcategories and the canonical t-structure on derived categories; adjoint functor theorems, mates and Verdier localization; the small étale site of a scheme with geometric points; algebraic cycles with a pushforward and orders of vanishing; and the algebra trace. Tau Ceti adds Weil and Cartier divisors with linear equivalence, field-level Kummer theory and discrete fixed-point trace formulas. Genuinely missing: constructible and ctf derived categories with derived ⊗ and RHom, Rf_!, f^!, dualizing complexes and Verdier biduality, trace maps and Poincaré duality, Chow groups, Chern and cycle classes and Gysin maps, weak Lefschetz and the projective-bundle and blowup formulas, the heart-is-abelian theorem, recollement, perverse sheaves and IC complexes, the ℓ-adic and Betti comparisons, the decomposition theorem and relative hard Lefschetz, and Lefschetz–Verdier traces for correspondences.

targets.target: Algebraic cycles and Chow groups with proper pushforward, flat pullback, rational equivalence and moving/deformation lemmas
targets.note: Mathlib defines cycles as locally finitely supported functions on points with a weighted pushforward along quasi-compact morphisms (only map_id is proved) and orders of vanishing at codimension-one points; Tau Ceti has Weil divisors mapping to cycles and proves O(D) ≅ O(E) iff D and E are linearly equivalent for locally principal divisors. Missing: Chow groups, rational equivalence beyond divisors, flat pullback, intersection products and moving lemmas.

targets.note: Searched perverse, perversity: nothing.
